subject: Estimating new indices with pre trained Mirt model (predicting)

messages.author: 6a2f2f09727dda68
messages.subject: Estimating new indices with pre trained Mirt model (predicting)
parts:
Greetings, everyone.

I have a trained IRT GRM model which I use to measure a construct based on a questionnaire/instrument. 

The thing is, I have a few more observations arriving late, and I would like to use the parameters from my previously trained model to estimate the theta of these new observations.

So basically, thinking in Machine Learning terms, what I need is a prediction for a new response, without the need to ajust a new model.

My data structure is the following:
I have a data.table object with the subjects' ID and the items they've answered on the questionnaire. My code to train/fit the model is the following:

grm_mod <- mirt::mirt(
  df[, .SD, .SDcols = -'SUBJECT_ID']
  , model = paste0('INDEX = ', first(items), ' - ', last(items))
  , itemtype = 'graded'
  , SE = T
)

Where items is a vector indicating which items to consider.

I have tried a solution that I've seen here, but didn't work: https://groups.google.com/g/mirt-package/c/QZbzozxO9H0/m/UVjUGXoOBAAJ

You should be able to use your previously fitted model and pass this to fscores() with the argument response.pattern=your_new_responses. No need to construct a new model in this case, though of course that's possible too.

Phil

Thanks! I eventually came across that solution. Just for the record, it looked like this:

pars <- data.table(
  a1 = grm_itm$a
  , d1 = grm_itm$d1
  , d2 = grm_itm$d2
  , d3 = grm_itm$d3
  , d4 = grm_itm$d4
)

model <- generate.mirt_object(parameters = pars, itemtype = 'graded')

theta <- fscores(object = model, response.pattern = df[, -'ID'])
